system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Seoul, South Korea. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Seoul itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Seoul space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Samcheong/Bukchon, Seochon/Tongui, Hannam/Itaewon, Cheongdam/Apgujeong, Euljiro/Jung-gu, Seongsu, Yeonhui/Mapo) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Seoul spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Seoul, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Kukje Gallery
galleries.note: Korea’s leading international gallery, with a blue-chip programme, major institutional reach and decades of Art Basel participation.

galleries.name: Gallery Hyundai
galleries.note: Founded in 1970, it helped build Korea’s modern gallery system and remains central to Dansaekhwa and contemporary art.

galleries.name: PKM Gallery
galleries.note: A highly respected Korean gallery with a rigorous international programme and sustained institutional and art-fair visibility.

galleries.name: Pace Gallery
galleries.note: The Seoul branch of a global blue-chip gallery, presenting major international and Korean artists in museum-scale exhibitions.

galleries.name: Lehmann Maupin
galleries.note: Longstanding Seoul outpost of an influential international gallery with an especially strong Korean and Asian programme.

galleries.name: Thaddaeus Ropac Seoul
galleries.note: Ambitious Seoul space for one of Europe’s most powerful galleries, regularly mounting historically significant exhibitions.

galleries.name: White Cube Seoul
galleries.note: The Seoul branch of the internationally influential London-founded gallery, with a major global artist roster.

galleries.name: Art Sonje Center
galleries.note: A foundational Korean contemporary-art institution known for influential commissions, exhibitions and curatorial experimentation.

galleries.name: Gana Art
galleries.note: One of Korea’s largest and longest-running commercial galleries, with significant domestic infrastructure and fair presence.

galleries.name: Arario Gallery Seoul
galleries.note: An influential Korean gallery and collecting enterprise with a strong record of developing major Asian contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Perrotin Seoul
galleries.note: A prominent branch of the global gallery, combining internationally recognizable artists with an active Korean programme.

galleries.name: Hakgojae Gallery
galleries.note: Important for connecting Korean art history, Dansaekhwa and contemporary practice through a sustained scholarly programme.

galleries.name: SongEun
galleries.note: A major nonprofit platform with an architecturally distinguished space, ambitious exhibitions and longstanding support for emerging Korean artists.

galleries.name: Jason Haam
galleries.note: A closely watched Korean gallery whose concentrated programme has rapidly gained international critical and fair visibility.

galleries.name: Esther Schipper Seoul
galleries.note: Seoul branch of the conceptually driven Berlin gallery, representing many institutionally prominent international artists.

galleries.name: Sprüth Magers Seoul
galleries.note: The Seoul outpost of a highly influential gallery known for conceptually rigorous, historically important artists.

galleries.name: Almine Rech Seoul
galleries.note: A global blue-chip gallery presenting prominent postwar and contemporary artists in its permanent Seoul space.

galleries.name: Mendes Wood DM Seoul
galleries.note: Internationally respected for a cross-generational, research-led programme connecting Latin America, Europe and Asia.

galleries.name: MASSIMODECARLO Seoul
galleries.note: The Seoul space of the influential Italian gallery, bringing a strong international roster into dialogue with the Korean market.

galleries.name: Gladstone Seoul
galleries.note: Permanent Seoul branch of a major international gallery known for critically established and museum-level artists.

galleries.name: ONE AND J. Gallery
galleries.note: A key advocate for Korean contemporary artists, with sustained international art-fair participation and curatorial credibility.

galleries.name: Gallery Baton
galleries.note: Respected for a sharply edited international programme and for introducing emerging and mid-career artists to Korea.

galleries.name: Whistle
galleries.note: One of Seoul’s most closely followed younger galleries, with an experimental programme and growing international fair presence.

galleries.name: P21
galleries.note: Influential compact gallery known for discovering younger Korean artists and placing them in wider international conversations.

galleries.name: Tang Contemporary Art Seoul
galleries.note: The Seoul branch of a major Asian gallery network, with a broad programme and substantial regional art-fair presence.

galleries.name: Johyun Gallery Seoul

galleries.name: Leeahn Gallery Seoul
galleries.note: Established Korean gallery with strong postwar and contemporary rosters and regular participation in international fairs.

galleries.name: Space K Seoul

galleries.name: Atelier Hermès

galleries.name: DOOSAN Gallery Seoul

galleries.name: Gallery2

galleries.name: 313 Art Project

galleries.name: Gallery Chosun

galleries.name: Art Space Pool

galleries.name: Insa Art Space

galleries.name: Project Space Sarubia

galleries.name: Platform-L Contemporary Art Center

galleries.name: Cylinder

galleries.name: N/A

galleries.name: Space Willing N Dealing

galleries.name: Artspace Boan 1942

galleries.name: WESS

galleries.name: Hall1

galleries.name: Gallery SP

galleries.name: Gallery Simon

galleries.name: Gallery BK
